canonical_statement: A probability law mu on finite-dimensional real Euclidean space is infinitely divisible if and only if its characteristic function has a Levy-Khintchine representation with a drift vector, a positive-semidefinite covariance operator, and a Levy measure, using the fixed truncation x * 1_{norm x <= 1}.

canonical_formal_target.planned_signature: For mu : ProbabilityMeasure (EuclideanSpace Real (Fin d)), InfinitelyDivisible mu iff there exist b, Q, nu satisfying the Levy-measure conditions and the stated characteristic-exponent identity for every frequency.

domain_and_universes: planned: d : Nat; mu a Borel probability measure on EuclideanSpace Real (Fin d); all objects in Lean universe 0
quantifiers: mu : Borel probability measure on R^d
representation data b : R^d, Q : positive-semidefinite symmetric operator, nu : Levy measure
hypotheses: nu({0}) = 0 and integral min(1, norm(x)^2) dnu(x) is finite
Q is symmetric and positive semidefinite
conclusion: mu is infinitely divisible iff its characteristic function equals exp(i*<b,u> - (1/2)*<u,Q u> + integral (exp(i*<u,x>) - 1 - i*<u,x>*1_{norm x <= 1}) dnu(x)) for every u

convention_freeze.fourier_sign: characteristic function uses exp(+i * inner u x)
